ateret-zekenim/1:_: And one does not wash hands at all, etc. But according to us, who wash all year before Kiddush, even now he should wash hands before Kiddush by rinsing his feet and not recite a berachah, and then for dipping he does not even need washing (Maharshal in responsa siman 86):
ateret-zekenim/5:_: These are vegetables with which a person fulfills [the mitzvah] — eighteen endives that they call in Polish zarzowich (Maharam Isserles and Akiva b. Meir wrote that he found in a medical book that there is no connection with the herb called zarzach as Maharam Isserles wished to explain):
biur-halacha/1:_: Until he began — see in Mishna Berurah what we wrote that for us even before they began the law is likewise, and this is from the words of the Gra; and the Gra exaggerated further that even if he remembered before eating karpas he may eat karpas without havdalah for this reason. And this detail is seemingly not so clear, for the law of adding to the cups through a berachah is not mentioned in all poskim, only in the words of Ravyah and the implication of Tur in siman 472 that for Rosh there is no rule for this between the first two cups, even when he blesses; and if so, perhaps it is better not to be concerned for this concern and not to taste before havdalah, which is a clear prohibition according to all, especially since perhaps even Avi Ezri agrees that havdalah proves on this cup that it was not brought to add on the cups; and the law requires further study:
biur-halacha/3:_: Permission is in his hand — and all this is between the cups; but if he poured the cup and began to expound on it in the Haggadah he is not permitted to interrupt in the middle — so Ramban in his hasagot, and so Ran; and it appears from his words even more that even if he has not yet begun the Haggadah, only that he poured the cup and prepared himself to say the Haggadah, it is also forbidden; and Baal HaMaor permits in all cases, and so Tosafot daf 103 that only in Hallel or in the berachah "who redeemed us" is it forbidden; and Mechaber was silent in seif 1 like the view of Ramban, even regarding a cup of mitzvah, and all the more a cup of permission; see in Beur HaGra there sk 4:
biur-halacha/5:_: He takes wormwood — see in Mishna Berurah that we explained in the words of the gloss that wormwood is not among the five species of maror, and so is proven in the long Darkei Moshe see there in his explanation of the words of the Agur. However Magen Avraham and Shach disagreed with him and proved that the Agur's intent is that wormwood is one of the five species of maror and is the maror mentioned last among the five species; and in my humble opinion it requires further study, for as it appears wormwood is not fit for eating, as implied from several verses that describe every evil thing with wormwood, as written "a root bearing gall and wormwood" or "its end bitter as wormwood," and we require something fit for eating by a person in any case, as explained in the words of Riaz and Ritva and as also proven from the Gemara that we require something purchasable with ma'aser money, unless impossible — then it is fit in any case somewhat for eating. Afterward I found in Rashbatz in Sefer Yavin Shemuah that he wrote explicitly one does not fulfill with wormwood because it is a type of tree and we require from types of vegetables, as we learned explicitly "these vegetables," etc., and so explained in the Gemara that it challenges "perhaps bitter caper," etc., and this is not like the view of Magen Avraham and not like the view of the gloss, for even if we say it has sap and one's face is ashamed, as we explained in Mishna Berurah, nevertheless these signs help only for a vegetable. Unless Rama did not write to fulfill with it as law but only as a general remembrance when one lacks the five species, and as the Gra also wrote; and the law requires further study. And know further that the sign that it has sap and one's face is ashamed — even though Rif and Rambam and Rosh omitted it, nevertheless it is mentioned in several poskim; see Riaz and Rashbatz and Maharam Chalavah who brought this sign for law; and in Beit Meir he wrote perhaps even Rif and those with him omitted it only because we are not expert in these signs well; therefore though it is difficult to bless based on these signs, nevertheless if one lacks the five species he should certainly seek any bitter species of vegetables that has the sign of sap and face ashamed, provided it is fit for eating by a person. And behold per what I wrote above on maror, if we require it be fit for eating, I now found in Peri Megadim he is somewhat doubtful whether one fulfills with maror even if not fit for eating, and he did not see the words of the aforementioned Rishonim; also the simple sense of the Gemara that we require it be purchasable with ma'aser money, as above (and see Rashi there); and what was difficult for him on the Gemara's challenge "perhaps bitter caper" — one may say this is the second answer of the Gemara even per the view that we do not require purchasability with ma'aser money; but nevertheless it is not at all produce of the ground; but for the conclusion in truth we do not need the Gemara's change of "produce of the ground," and such is the way of sugyot in many places:
biur-halacha/6:א: (א) Less than a kezayit — from here it implies that something dipped in liquid requires washing even for less than a kezayit, even for plain bread; Mechaber wrote in siman 158 seif 3 in the name of some that washing is not required for less than a kezayit, and this is not as we wrote there in Mishna Berurah sk 20; and I already noted this in the second printing in the margins; but now I found a Tanna who supports my words — namely Rashbatz in Sefer Yavin Shemuah 4:35, who wrote regarding karpas that according to Rambam we require a kezayit, and he wrote it is reasonable that since washing is required, certainly a kezayit is required, like eating plain bread — it is reasonable he is not obligated in washing, for certainly they did not decree in such a case because of concern for terumah; and likewise for fruits in something dipped in liquid; and Mateh Yehudah brought it exactly as our words; and the law requires further study:
biur-halacha/6:ב: (ב) And he does not bless afterward — see in Mishna Berurah; and the Gra wrote in his beur that all this is according to Mechaber's view in siman 474 that he blesses only one berachah on the first two cups, and because Hallel and the Haggadah are not an interruption, therefore he does not bless birkat hamazon — for he relies on the berachah of karpas to eat maror without a berachah; but per the gloss and our custom that he blesses each cup and cup, one cannot rely on the berachah of the first cup because he interrupted with Hallel and the Haggadah; and if so one cannot say we rely in eating maror on the berachah of karpas, since he interrupted with the Haggadah and Hallel (only maror is exempt from a berachah because it is like things that come within the meal, which are dismissed by the berachah of hamotzi); and if so he is obligated to bless birkat hamazon after eating karpas, since it is not related to the meal that comes afterward — this is the essence of the Gra's words. And in truth Rav Magen Avraham was careful about this and wrote in siman 474 that each cup requires a berachah according to all, even for one who holds the Haggadah and Hallel are not an interruption, and because each mitzvah is separate therefore he must bless on each (and as Rif wrote at the beginning of his words in the name of the rabbis); and per Magen Avraham's words the Gra's words are rejected, and as Magen Avraham wrote, many Acharonim wrote above in siman 278 seif 6 except Taz — see there; and one may say this reasoning applies here too, that karpas and maror are two mitzvot and therefore one does not exempt the other; and the law requires further study:
chatam-sofer/1:_: (There in Magen Avraham sk 4) Maharil wrote they are accustomed to take karpas — n.b. in Greek and Latin: apia. And notarikon: El — O Worker of salvations are You; and in foreign tongue seller; and see Chiddushei Sofer Orach Chayim siman 132:
chatam-sofer/2:_: In Mechaber seif 5 tamcha — n.b. notarikon: always tell the glory of the Almighty; and see responsa Orach Chayim siman 132 [there it is written in this language about the mitzvot of matzah and maror on Pesach — truly correct is what Chacham Tzvi wrote (and it is in siman 119), and the content of his words is that the chazeret mentioned in our Mishnah and in the language of the Sages is chasa, which is the head, and the first head mentioned in the Mishnah; and the mitzvah to return to it is the vegetable called in our country (salad), and so all my rabbis of blessed memory practiced and we practice after them; but I am accustomed to preach on Shabbat HaGadol: one who lacks designated people of fear who inspect and clean it of swarms of tiny worms found very much in Pesach days and not visible to weak eyes — therefore one who lacks in his house someone to inspect it properly should dip and take tamcha called horseradish; and if it is the third in the Mishnah and chasa is the first, nevertheless it is preferable from anywhere — Heaven forbid to stumble in a prohibition or many prohibitions even in safeik because of fulfilling a positive rabbinic mitzvah of maror in our time, which is rabbinic, especially since both can be fulfilled through tamcha] and we fulfill with stalks even dry and also with leaves — the view of Peri Chadash is that one fulfills with dried, and it is known by sense that dried and withered do not retain their taste in it and its smell is bitter much more than pickled in water from time to time, which Magen Avraham forbids below sk 14 and Kaf HaChayyim disagrees that water does not nullify taste, only pickling in vinegar; nevertheless it is also clear that honey is worse than pickling in vinegar so that it stands on the fire and begins to boil; and therefore it must be that there it is different, for bitter taste emerges through another power mixed in, namely the power of vinegar or even only water, unlike as long as the vegetable is by itself without another power it does not lose as long as some of its own bitterness is tasted — unlike dried leaves for those who forbid; and this is the reason they are accustomed to salt tamcha to nullify its bitterness somewhat so they can eat a kezayit of it; and so when we reclined at the table our master the pious one of priestly lineage, the honor of our teacher R. Nathan Adler, in the year 5545 in Vienna, no chasa was found for dipping without worms, and he commanded to salt tamcha and we ate it; and I expanded on this unlike the words of the Gaon in the Haggadah miracle story at first that the Gemara Berachot 39a forbids prima prima zita to sweeten taste — it is a fortiori from boiling in water see there; and per my view his a fortiori does not apply. And further it appears to me that if possible to eat Pesach and matzah with wormwood or even tamcha, which is not the normal way of eating, as Rambam wrote that mixing a bitter thing is not the normal way of eating — rather they nullify taste through prima zuta; and see below siman 475 in Magen Avraham sk 10; and in truth crushed tamcha dipped in vinegar is eaten thus, and it must be if one soaks it in vinegar again he should not bless on eating maror anyway after he filled his belly he should not bless again on eating maror:
chatam-sofer/3:_: (There in Magen Avraham sk 14 in the matter of) Maharil wrote, etc., and all the more when rooted — n.b. and per Tosafot Rosh Hashanah 13a that a non-Jew has rights in what he planted — one may say a vegetable that does not last and is sown all year a non-Jew has rights, unlike a tree that lasts, for perhaps it still stands from its original owners and is not stolen — it is simple. However one should examine Bava Metzia 101b because of denial of land see there; and examine carefully:
chatam-sofer/4:_: (There) in Mechaber seif 7 so that they will ask — n.b. the language of Rambam chapter 8 law 2: "and here the son asks and says; the reader: why is this night different," etc. — it implies the reader of the Haggadah says "why is this night different." And in the Gemara it implies if the son asks the reader should not say but rather "we were slaves:"
chatam-sofer/5:_: (There) in Magen Avraham sk 29 called ah"ch — n.b. yud-vav hei-kaf, meaning etzba (finger); gematria 163 in milui Y-H-V-H; and on the finger ten plagues reach — each plague sixteen, and three hundreds which are the weapons of sixteen; and the tablets with the finger of the Almighty reach — each utterance sixteen, as the Sages said: the sword and the book descended rolled from heaven:
chokhmat-shlomo/5:_: Seif 5 — These are the vegetables with which one fulfills his obligation, etc. Note: we read in Pesachim daf 39b: Rambach asked whether one fulfills with ma'aser sheni for maror, etc., until Rava said it is reasonable — matzah and maror with Yom Tov — see my explanation of this sugya in my books on Orach Chayim from the year 5622 in the laws of Birkat HaMazon siman 184, in my writings there daf 131a — see there and investigate.(There, seif 5 in the gloss) And if he lacks one of these vegetables he takes wormwood or another bitter vegetable, etc. Note: it appears clear to me that one may take radish called rettich in our country for maror, for it is explicit in Magen Avraham and Beit Yosef that tamcha is what they call maraytikh; and if in Ashkenaz they call krien rettich, nevertheless rettich too is so called; if so, both are called thus — only to distinguish they call one maraytikh and one rettich, but their root is one; reason supports this, for radish too is pungent like krien, soft at first and hard at end, a sharp thing like krien; and Rama's view is that otherwise one fulfills with any bitter vegetable, and Rashi in Chumash as Magen Avraham wrote. This does not contradict the mishnah — one may say: for matzah types where the Torah specifies importance, only these five count as bread; but maror is not specified in Torah what it is, therefore Rashi explained from Torah any bitter herb is maror, but the Sages enumerated those common in their place, soft beginning hard end — they found these and enumerated them. Similarly Megillah 10: why did the Sages enumerate these, etc. — they found these and enumerated, not only these; so too maror — they found these and enumerated; and if another similar species is found it is also maror; therefore Rashi: since Torah did not specify the species, whatever is a bitter vegetable is called maror — unlike matzah where Torah requires chimutz and it be called bread, and Torah specified bread is only wheat and barley — therefore for matzah we need specifically these; not so maror; therefore for rettich, which we doubt if in tamcha category, there is room to say perhaps in tamcha; and if you say not in tamcha, perhaps per Rashi and Rama one fulfills with any thing. The essential view: both krien and rettich are in tamcha category and are one species as explained — several elders told me they saw people fulfill maror with rettich; investigate.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: [1] [Levush] And one need not wash, etc. So wrote Rama, and Taz agreed, and so is widespread custom not to wash; and if hands are not clean he washes a little but does not recite on washing; for first dipping wash without berakha, for second dipping wash with berakha. What Magen Avraham challenged — that all year one does not wash hands for dipping — is no difficulty, as Levush wrote seif 6; and this is Maharil's wording: if one washes before kiddush it appears the law is like Beit Shammai who washes hands and then sanctifies — until here. So he explained what Darkei Moshe wrote — that Beit Shammai's view is kiddush requires washing, meaning they wash before pouring the cup, i.e., kiddush; investigate, for I abbreviated; Magen Avraham wondered in vain; Ma'agalei Tzedek wrote the reason: Hagadah recitation is an interruption between washing and eating.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: [2] And he makes kiddush, etc. And if he forgot, his law is as above siman 471 seif 8; but if he forgot to say Hagadah he has no compensation, for it is written "because of this" when matzah and maror are placed before you (later authorities).
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: [3] Sheheheyanu, etc. Chok Yaakov wrote: if he did not bless on the first night and they said it on the second night, he fulfills either way — if the first was holy he completed on the second day; if the first was weekday he need not complete; if they said on the first and not the second, he blesses all seven when he remembers; see siman 494 s"k.
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: [4] [Levush] Because he will say, etc. Maharil wrote one does not recite she-asah nissim except on a rabbinic mitzvah like Chanukah and Purim; Matah Moshe wrote in the name of Rav Amram that it is a day of salvation and preferable to miracles.
eliyah-rabbah/5:_: [5] [Levush] Havdalah, etc. Seated (Matah Moshe), like Hallel all year standing and on Pesach night sitting because of reclining and freedom as written end of siman 422; therefore one should not stand even at the beginning of Vaykhulu.
eliyah-rabbah/6:_: [6] [Levush] The seven havdalot, etc. In Avudraham he explained: between holy and profane, light and darkness, Israel and nations — behold three; "between the seventh day and six days of work" is not counted but since we say it generally we say it here; between sanctity of Shabbat and sanctity of Yom Tov you distinguished — this is ochel nefesh permitted on Yom Tov, behold four; "and the seventh day from six days of work you sanctified" — this is the last Yom Tov of the festival separated from the six intermediate days — behold five; "and You distinguished Your people," etc. — are two distinctions between kohanim and levi'im and levi'im and Israelites; difficulty: where are the six intermediate days — strained to reconcile.
eliyah-rabbah/7:_: [7] And afterward he makes havdalah, etc. Then he makes havdalah on the cup; if he remembered in the middle of the meal he makes havdalah immediately on the cup and does not recite borei peri hagafen; if he forgot until after Birkat HaMazon he says Hallel and havdalah on one cup, since it is impossible otherwise.
eshel-avraham/4:_: And two cooked dishes. Tur concludes even if Pesach falls on the first day of Yom Tov; see Ba'er Heitev chapter 1:6 and Likutei 8:71 siman 22, who challenged Tur's words against each other.
eshel-avraham/6:_: that the women understand. The women really are not obligated to the saying of the Haggadah which is a MA that the ZAG even though they were in the same miracle this date does not belong in the Mitzva Dauriita and it will not be but a sukkah even though they were also covered in a cloud. Rather, a didan is to tell them the miracles and wonders of the Omnipresent.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] They pour for him the first cup, etc. And the cups require rinsing and washing, for they are cups of berakha — Drashot Maharil Seder Ha'agadah; Rokeach siman 283; and so Mahariv in the name of Maharai and Beit Yosef Darchei Moshe in siman 486 s"k 2; and Chayei Adam kelal 130 s"k 10 wrote: if they are clean, rinsing and washing between cups are not needed, only rinsing the first cup suffices — end of his words; nevertheless see above siman 183 seif 1 and our words there s"k 4, that per Zohar and tikkunim a Birkat HaMazon cup requires washing and rinsing even if clean — see there; nevertheless it is good to have a vessel full of water near the table to rinse and wash cups between cup and cup. Sefer HaMitzvot; Tosafot Chayim on Chayei Adam there s"k 34; and see further below s"k 142 and siman 479 s"k 1.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (2) There. They pour the first cup, etc. See above siman 472 s"k 58 and below siman 474 s"k 2.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (3) There. And he makes kiddush on it, etc. And before kiddush one should say this text: for the sake of the unification of Kudsha Berikh Hu (vav heh yod heh vav heh) in fear and love (yod heh yod heh vav heh heh) love and fear (aleph heh heh yod vav heh heh) to unify the name yod heh with vav heh in complete unity (yod heh vav heh) in the name of all Israel and in the name of every soul, spirit, and living nefesh, unique soul related to the roots of our nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah, yechidah, garments, those close and attached, from the totality of Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah and every detail of ABY"A — each parzuf and sefirah of ABY"A details — behold we come to fulfill with intent all mitzvot operative this night, the Pesach night, first night of the Festival of Matzot: mitzvah of kiddush on the first wine cup; mitzvah of first hand-washing for karpas dipping; eating karpas; rabbinic mitzvah of telling the Exodus, as written "and you shall tell your son on that day," etc.; berakha of redemption on the second wine cup; second netilat yadayim for the meal; berakha of netilat yadayim; ha-motzi and eating matzah; rabbinic mitzvah of eating matzah as written "in the evening you shall eat matzot"; eating maror to remember Egyptian bitterness and dipping in charoset in remembrance of clay; korekh matzah and maror together per Hillel the Elder; eating afikoman in remembrance of the Pesach offering; final hand-washing; rabbinic Birkat HaMazon; also saying on the third wine cup; mitzvah of reading Hallel and drinking the fourth wine cup — to repair the root of all these mitzvot in the supernal place through the hidden and concealed. And may the pleasantness, etc.
kaf-hachayyim/4:א: (א) There. And he makes kiddush on it. See above siman 472 s"k 51 that we wrote the first cup corresponds to chochmah of binah — see there; on the first cup intend that the cup itself is gematria Elohim; nevertheless intend its exchanged aspect (meaning the letters of Elohim exchange with preceding letters per some, and some say they do not exchange) — the name AKDaT"M; the five fingers of the right hand correspond to the five letters AKDaT"M; wine in the cup also hints AKDaT"M, for wine is gematria 70, and with the five fingers holding it behold 75, count of AKDaT"M with the kollel; in the havayah of the kiddush berakha intend the name 72, aspect of chochmah.
kaf-hachayyim/4:ב: (ב) And the second cup is aspect of binah of binah; intend in it the name AKDa"M divided into two mems gimel lamed (meaning AKDa"M is gematria gimel lamed); in the havayah of Asher Ga'alanu intend the name 63, aspect of binah.
kaf-hachayyim/4:ג: (ג) And the two final cups are in the aspects of chesed and gevurah of da'at; therefore between the third and fourth one should not drink, so as not to separate them. The first cup is chesed of da'at — intend AKDa"M in its calculation, gematria 74, with kollel 75, which is also yud beit kuf (meaning threefold havayah Elohim, each gematria yud beit kuf); and the name 45, aspect of chesed of da'at. The last cup is gevurot of da'at — intend AKDa"M in its calculation gematria 74 and the name 52, aspect of gevurot of da'at. You should join both intentions in the first cup, then return to intend both in the second cup, as explained in Sha'ar HaKavanot and Pri Etz Chayim chapters 2–3 — see there.
kaf-hachayyim/5:א: (1) e) Name. and a temple on him. Yekadesh Ma'amed. Sadhi. And we do not practice that unless Passover falls on Shabbat because they could. As mentioned in the Haga'a and so on in his book Pesach Ma'ovin O' Rach. Indeed, per the words of the late Ari Zal, all the Kiddoshin Tzal are placed between Shabbat's and YoT's Kmash above C. Re'a O' Sab Yaush and K. K. Hipl 12 O' 1 and wrote there and beginning these the days of the the Master Etc. If it falls on a holiday, then you will eat it. But if it falls on Shabbat, first of all, say the day of the Friday and eat, etc. And then these are the days of the the Master, etc. and then my thoughts. And then the blessing of the wine and the blessing of kiddush today and that we live. And first of all, a psalm to David H. Rui, etc.
kaf-hachayyim/5:ב: (ב) And know there is no Torah-ordained Yom Tov kiddush, as above siman 471 s"k 6 — see there; and further see above siman 472 s"k 83.
kaf-hachayyim/6:_: (6) There. And he recites sheheheyanu, etc. With this he is exempt from reciting sheheheyanu on matzah — Mahari Molcho in responsum 36; Rabbeinu Yerucham s"k 1; therefore when saying sheheheyanu on kiddush, intend to exempt the mitzvah of eating matzah; see below siman 643 seif 1.
kaf-hachayyim/7:_: (7) And that one does not recite ha-tov ve-ha-metiv on the festival — because this good is not shared with another; it is comparable to rain fell and he has no field in partnership — investigate siman 221 that I do not recite — Mahari Molcho responsum 36 siman 101; Birkei Yosef s"k 2; and Leket Yosher vol. 1 siman 58 wrote: in place of ha-tov ve-ha-metiv they enacted tefillat and in kiddush "You chose us," etc. — there is no greater good — see there.
netiv-chayim/1:_: (Magen Avraham seif kaf 13) It implies that one does not fulfill with wilted ones; Mishna Berurah: so wrote Riaz in the name of the Yerushalmi chapter 2 halachah 5 that leaves are invalid — and this is a very great stringency, for how will he act properly? If in water we are concerned for pickled; if he leaves it without water we are concerned for wilted — go out and see what the public does, for they are accustomed to fulfill with wilted ones. And in order to reconcile the custom I searched the source of the law in the Yerushalmi, and this is its language: "between wilted" (meaning it refers to the mishnah that reads "between wilted") — there is a baraita: two, but not wilted. Rav Chisda said: the one who says wilted [applies] to the stalk, and the one who says not wilted [applies] to the leaves, end of his words. And from this he ruled that one does not fulfill with wilted leaves. And behold, this is per the text of the Yerushalmi that reads in the mishnah "between wilted," which requires resolving the baraita so it should not contradict the mishnah; but according to our text that reads "between dry ones," one can say the baraita comes according to one opinion and we rule like R' Meir and his colleagues and like Ra'avad, and so I found in Ra'avan page 73 that one fulfills with wilted ones. And further, since R' Eliezer said only in the stalk, but in leaves moist ones — not dry ones — from that R' Eliezer said "dry" and did not say "wilted," it implies wilted ones are valid; the truth was to explain his words as Rashbam wrote in Pesachim page 101 s.v. lekiv'a kama, etc.; and that which he said "moist" is not precise, as the Rosh wrote in the chapter of stolen lulav siman 10 see there — and therefore the poskim omitted this law, for they did not need it: individual and many — the halachah is like the many, and examine:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: Magen Avraham seif kaf 2 until after the meal — nevertheless he is obligated to interrupt his meal and recite Havdalah, since he began in prohibition — see Magen Avraham siman 471 seif 12:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/2:_: Magen Avraham seif kaf 4 And I wonder why we are not accustomed [to take] from Yerushalmi chapter 9 of Shevi'it, brought in Tosafot chapter 9 mishnah 5 of Shabbat: what is karpas in the rivers of Bavel? Petroselinon:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/3:_: Magen Avraham seif kaf 8 That Yom Tov does not prepare for its fellow — it is not understood, for in any case on the night of the second Yom Tov too he will not eat it; and if he would eat it on the day of the second Yom Tov — only that generally he will not eat it on the first day of Yom Tov since he needs it for the night of the second Yom Tov; if so, what relevance is there, in the introduction that one does not eat roasted and therefore it is forbidden? In any case, since he wishes to keep it for the second night and does not wish to eat it on the first, it is forbidden to roast it:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/4:_: Magen Avraham seif kaf 14 Everything standing to be uprooted is considered as uprooted — it does not suffice, for even now when it is fully cooked it is considered uprooted; nevertheless the gentile did not now acquire it and did not become a robber on it, as is stated in Bava Kamma 117b, brought in Magen Avraham below siman 637; and if so, when the Jew uproots he is the robber and there is no change of ownership:
shaarei-teshuvah/2:_: On Shabbat, Avodat HaTodah and in Iggerot HaRamaz siman 13 he wrote, and this is its language: and regarding the matter of commerce and telling of the Exodus from Egypt — it is obvious to me that it is forbidden if the person is alone without guarding, end of his words — and it is astonishing, for it is against Shulchan Aruch siman 475; and it is possible it does not refer to telling the Haggadah but only that he wishes to tell, and it requires study:
yad-ephraim/1:_: 473 in Taz seif kaf 1: he should wash hands at the second dipping. And he explains there reasons, etc.; and Tosafot explained this second dipping, etc.; and in truth it is not fitting for him to bless now on Pesach, for he will bless to wash again for bread — they do not fulfill with this washing because of the interruption, etc., so it should be:
yad-ephraim/2:_: (Taz seif kaf 4) for it is impossible roasted, end of his words, and I did not see, etc. — thus they do not eat; also what the Mechaber wrote about the egg, etc., so it should be:
yad-ephraim/3:_: In Magen Avraham seif kaf 14 it is not established in the ground — it is like movable property, and gentiles acquire through abandonment, and there is change of ownership in the hand of the Jew, so it should be:
yad-ephraim/4:_: In Taz seif kaf 7 Tur wrote and R' Meir of Rothenburg wrote that nowadays, etc.; and the Rambam's reason because there is no washing, etc.; and one should greatly wonder on the Levush who wrote that on this night, etc., that if he had not dipped except the second of maror it would not have been recognizable, so it should be:
